preamble: The palatal lateral [ʎ], with tongue-body contact on the hard palate, shifts to the palatalized alveolar lateral [lʲ], with apical contact at the alveolar ridge and a secondary palatal gesture. Proto-Slavic *ľ (from *lj) is usually reconstructed as a true palatal [ʎ]. In East Slavic it merged with the secondarily palatalized [lʲ] that arose before front vowels, so Proto-Slavic *voľa 'will' gives Russian and Ukrainian volja with [lʲ], while Serbo-Croatian keeps the palatal in vȍlja [ʎ].
phoneticEffects: Depalatalization of Primary Place, Secondary Palatalization, Merger

examples.note: Proto-Slavic *ľ merged with the palatalized lateral; cf. Serbo-Croatian vȍlja, which keeps [ʎ].
Same East Slavic merger of *ľ with [lʲ].

sources: Charles, S., & Lulich, S. M. (2019). Articulatory-acoustic relations in the production of alveolar and palatal lateral sounds in Brazilian Portuguese. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 145(6), 3269. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5109565
